estimate.damage_summary: A nearby atmospheric discharge caused an overvoltage event on the building’s electrical installation, physically damaging the speaker system and TV. A technician subsequently checked the surge failure and wiring safety.
estimate.policy_notes: The appliances are covered for established physical damage from lightning-related overvoltage under clauses 2.3.3 and 4.2.4, subject to the EUR 5,000 gross appliance sub-limit per event and the pre-loss-standard cap in 7.1.9. Because the appliances were not connected through surge-protective devices, clause 2.3.3 reduces indemnity for them by half; use payout_fraction 0.5. Diagnostic reports and contractor call-out charges are excluded under 7.1.8(d)–(e); attendance is not payable where the same invoice contains no indemnifiable work.

lines.invoice_text: Surge-damaged home electronics (speaker system and TV set)
lines.rationale: Clauses 2.3.3, 4.2.4 and 7.1.1 cover replacement of appliances with established physical damage from the reported overvoltage, while 7.1.9 limits payment to standard-grade equivalents of the pre-loss items. The two appliances are related and the invoiced quantity is plausible; the absence of surge protection halves otherwise payable indemnity under 2.3.3, and the EUR 5,000 gross sub-limit applies across the appliance claim.

lines.invoice_text: Diagnostic surge-failure report and technician call-out
lines.rationale: The diagnostic report is related to the surge event, but clause 7.1.8(e) excludes the contractor’s own diagnostics and reports; clause 7.1.8(d) excludes the accompanying call-out where the invoice contains no indemnifiable work. The three-unit quantity is recorded as invoiced, but neither the report nor attendance has a positive fair value under these clauses.
